faqs.question: When is Raksha Bandhan in 2026?
faqs.answer: Friday 28 August 2026. It is a restricted holiday on the official 2026 central holiday lists rather than a national public holiday, though several states treat it as a bank holiday.

faqs.question: How late can I post a personalised rakhi card and still have it arrive on time?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the Department of Posts' own standards: 1-2 days local and 4-5 days to the rest of the country by Speed Post, or 5-6 days by ordinary letter post. For 28 August 2026 that means posting by roughly 21 August inside India, and a week earlier if the address is remote.

faqs.question: Is a printed card or a digital card better for a brother living abroad?
faqs.answer: Digital, if the date matters. India Post's end-to-end EMS standards are 4-7 days to the United States, 5-9 to Canada and 4-8 to the UAE, and they exclude customs holding time, so an overseas card posted inside ten days is a gamble while a link arrives in seconds.

faqs.question: Can I put my brother's nickname on the card instead of his real name?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it usually works better. The name he answers to at home is what makes the card feel addressed to him rather than printed for anyone; a legal name nobody in the family uses reads like a form letter.

faqs.question: What should I write on a Raksha Bandhan card with his name on it?
faqs.answer: The name, one specific memory with a place or a year in it, and one concrete promise for the coming year. Skip the stock line: a CHI 2022 study of 18,559 pre-printed card messages found them heavily patterned by the recipient's gender, so the printed sentiment is the least personal thing on the card.

faqs.question: Can I make a personalised Raksha Bandhan card with a name for free?
faqs.answer: Yes on the digital route, where creating and sharing a name-personalised page costs nothing. A printed card always has a card price plus postage, and a photo upload is normally a paid upgrade on top.

faqs.question: Does my sister need an app or an account to open the link?
faqs.answer: No. A shared page opens in whatever browser is already on her phone, which matters because 51.9% of the 32,683 views recorded on SubhSandesh pages happen on a phone.

faqs.question: Can I keep the card private so it does not get forwarded?
faqs.answer: Password-protect it before you share. 44.3% of SubhSandesh creators do exactly that (1,205 of 2,718 pages), which for a sibling card is less about secrecy than about it not being reposted into a forty-person family group.

faqs.question: Can I add a photo as well as the name?
faqs.answer: Yes on both formats. On a digital card the photo is free and swappable; on a printed card a photo upload is a paid option and is fixed once you check out.

faqs.question: Do I have to finish the card in one sitting?
faqs.answer: No, and most people do not. The median gap between a SubhSandesh page's first save and its last edit is 6.9 hours, sampled across 913 pages of one template, so writing the name now and the message tonight is the normal pattern.

faqs.question: Is a card enough on its own, or should I send a gift too?
faqs.answer: The card is enough when it is genuinely specific to your sibling. A 2021 randomised study in The BMJ found that generic posted cards sent to 1,469 people changed response rates by nothing (85.3% versus 85.4%), which is a reminder that the personal content carries the card, not the paper.

faqs.question: Can I write the name in Hindi or Marathi script?
faqs.answer: On a digital card, yes: anything you can type on your phone's keyboard, including Devanagari, renders on the page. On a printed card it depends on whether that press supports the font, so check before ordering.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Personalised Raksha Bandhan Card With Name: Post It or Send It?

A personalised Raksha Bandhan card with a name is a card that carries your sibling's actual name — the one you call them at home, not the one on their Aadhaar — and you have exactly two ways to get it to them. Posted, it travels at the Department of Posts' published service standards: 1–2 days local, 4–5 days to the rest of the country, 4–7 days to the United States.

Sent as a link it arrives in seconds, and on SubhSandesh's own numbers 51.9% of the 32,683 recorded views of shared pages happen on a phone, while 44.3% of the 2,718 pages created since 12 March 2026 were password-protected before sharing. Raksha Bandhan falls on Friday 28 August 2026, so below is the lead-time maths, the five things the card has to carry beside the name, and the cases where paper still wins.

## What is a personalised Raksha Bandhan card with a name?

It is a Raksha Bandhan greeting whose text names one specific person — "For my brother Aarav" instead of "To my dear brother" — usually alongside a line only the two of you would understand. The name is the mechanism, not the decoration: it turns a mass-produced sentiment into an addressed one.

Two formats do this, and they behave differently. A printed card is personalised at the press and then posted, so the wording is frozen the moment you check out. A digital card is personalised in a browser, published to a private link and delivered over WhatsApp, email or a shared album — editable up to the minute you send it.

That editability matters more than it sounds. On SubhSandesh, 99.4% of started pages are actually published and shared (2,701 of 2,718), so the wording step is rarely where people abandon a card — running out of postal days is.

## The lead-time maths for Friday 28 August 2026

Raksha Bandhan 2026 falls on Friday 28 August, listed as a restricted holiday in [the official 2026 holiday list](https://cdnbbsr.s3waas.gov.in/s3kv050c109a2f75a8b2607737efd65509/uploads/2026/01/2026012982.pdf) issued in December 2025. That gives a card posted on 18 August ten days of runway, which sounds generous until you read the actual norms.

The [Department of Posts Citizens' Charter](https://www.indiapost.gov.in/documents/CitizenCharter2021.pdf) sets Speed Post at 1–2 days local, 1–3 days metro to metro, 1–4 days within a state and 4–5 days for the rest of the country. Ordinary first-class letter post — which is what most greeting cards travel as — is slower: 2 days local, 2–4 metro to metro, 3–5 between state capitals and 5–6 days for the rest of India.

International is where the plan usually breaks. The same charter gives end-to-end EMS standards of 2–6 days to the UK, 4–7 to the United States, 4–8 to the UAE and Australia, 5–9 to Canada and 3–6 to Singapore — explicitly excluding time held for customs examination, and only for articles booked in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai or Kochi. Book from anywhere else and the domestic leg is added on top.

Read together: inside India, ten days is enough if you post this week. For a brother in Toronto, 5–9 days plus customs against a 28 August deadline is a coin toss, and that is the case where a [Raksha Bandhan page for your brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) with his name on it beats a parcel, because it has no transit time at all.

## Five things a name-personalised rakhi card needs

Each item states what it is, who it suits, what it costs and how long it takes.

### 1. The name they actually answer to

What it is: the name used at home — Chhotu, Didi, Bhai, a school nickname — rather than the legal one. Who it suits: anyone whose sibling has a formal name nobody in the family uses.

Cost: nothing on either format. Time: under a minute, and it is the highest-return minute in the whole job, because a card addressed to "Aarav" and a card addressed to "Chhotu" are read as two different objects.

### 2. One dated memory instead of a stock line

What it is: a sentence naming a place, a year or an argument — "the 2019 Diwali you drove six hours to reach". Who it suits: siblings you have real history with, which is most of them.

Cost: nothing. Time: five to ten minutes of thinking, and worth it — a CHI 2022 study built a corpus of [18,559 stock greeting-card messages](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~sherryw/assets/pubs/2022-greeting_card.pdf) from eight card publishers and found them heavily patterned by the recipient's gender, which makes the pre-printed line the least personal thing on the card.

### 3. The protection promise in your own words

What it is: the rakshan half of Raksha Bandhan — the thread is a promise, so say what you are actually promising this year. Who it suits: cards for a younger sibling, and any card where "happy rakhi" alone feels thin.

Cost: nothing. Time: two minutes, and be concrete — "I will pick up the phone this year" is a promise, while "always there for you" is a greeting-card default.

### 4. A photo, or last year's thali

What it is: one image — the two of you, or the plate with the rakhi, roli and sweets from last year. Who it suits: siblings who have not been in the same room in months.

Cost: free on a digital card, while on printed cards a photo upload is normally a paid upgrade. Time: five minutes to find the file, which is usually the longest step.

### 5. A delivery route decided before you design anything

What it is: choosing post versus link first, because the choice dictates the format, the deadline and the length of the message. Who it suits: everyone, and it is the step most people skip.

Cost: nothing. Time: one minute, spent holding the charter windows above against today's date.

## Printed card, digital card or both

The comparison below uses the Citizens' Charter standards for transit and SubhSandesh's own view data for what happens after delivery.

| Option | Same city | Rest of India | Sibling in the USA | After it arrives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Card by first-class letter post | 2 days | 5–6 days | Not covered by the charter's standards | No reopen data exists |
| Card by Speed Post | 1–2 days | 4–5 days | 4–7 days, customs time excluded | Tracked to the door |
| Name-personalised page sent as a link | Seconds | Seconds | Seconds | 12.0 views per page on average, 51.9% of them on a phone |
| Link on the day, card posted after | Seconds, then 1–2 days | Seconds, then 4–5 days | Seconds, then 4–7 days | Meets the date and leaves an object |

The takeaway: paper is the better object and the worse courier, so if the date is inside a week and the sibling is overseas, send the link first and let the card arrive late on purpose.

## What belongs beside the name on the card

Most people underrate how much this lands. In a 2018 *Psychological Science* study, [107 MBA students wrote letters of gratitude](https://uploads-ssl.webflow.com/5c484e0f4aa6f839dc553c45/5c9a38dff7d06d3980dad2df_KumarEpley2018.pdf) and predicted their recipients' reactions; among the 80 recipients who responded, writers significantly underestimated how surprised and how positive the recipients felt (d = 0.74 for mood) and overestimated how awkward it would be.

The practical reading for a rakhi card: the sentence you are embarrassed to write is usually the one worth writing. Name the thing they did, not the category of thing.

Give yourself more than one sitting. On SubhSandesh the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.9 hours, sampled across 913 pages of one template — people write the name immediately and come back to the message later, which a printed card's checkout flow does not allow.

And decide who else can see it. 44.3% of creators password-protect the page before sharing, which for a sibling card is less about secrecy than about it not being forwarded into a family group of forty people. If you want to see how the finished thing reads before writing anything, the [SubhSandesh template gallery](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) shows the published versions.

## When a printed card beats a link — and when both lose

A physical card wins outright in three cases: the sibling is in the same city and you can hand it over, the sibling does not use a smartphone comfortably, or you want an object that survives a phone change. A link is a URL; a card is ephemera, and ephemera is what people find in a box twenty years later.

A card also does nothing on its own. In a randomised study published in *The BMJ* in December 2021, researchers sent Christmas cards to 1,469 trial participants across eight host trials and measured follow-up completion: [85.3% for the card group versus 85.4% for no card](https://www.bmj.com/content/375/bmj-2021-067742), at £0.76 and roughly 140 g of CO₂ equivalent per card.

Those were institutional cards to strangers, not a named card from a sibling. They are still a fair warning that the artefact is not the active ingredient — the name and the specific line are.

SubhSandesh is the wrong choice in the same-room case, and it is the wrong choice if your sibling reads nothing on a phone: 51.9% of views are mobile, which is a strength only when the recipient is one of those people. It is also the wrong choice if you want something framed — the page is not a print product, and it will not survive a dead link.

## Sources

- Department of Posts, *Citizens' Charter* (2021) — Speed Post, first-class mail and international EMS service standards.
- Coleman E, et al., "Bah humbug! Association between sending Christmas cards to trial participants and trial retention", *The BMJ*, 14 December 2021.
- Kumar A, Epley N, "Undervaluing Gratitude: Expressers Misunderstand the Consequences of Showing Appreciation", *Psychological Science* 29(9), 2018.
- Sun J, Wu T, Jiang Y, Awalegaonkar R, Lin XV, Yang D, "Pretty Princess vs. Successful Leader: Gender Roles in Greeting Card Messages", *CHI 2022*, 29 April 2022.
- Kendriya Vidyalaya list of holidays for 2026 (issued 22 December 2025) — Raksha Bandhan on 28 August 2026.

failed.why: Only partially verifiable at write time. Three sibling files existed when this was checked (how-to-tie-rakhi-virtually-on-video-call, raksha-bandhan-whatsapp-status-with-name, raksha-bandhan-wishes-with-name-and-photo) and none of them shares a URL or a domain with this post's four sources; six of the ten batch posts were still being drafted concurrently, so a full batch-wide count was impossible. indiapost.gov.in is the one plausible collision, being an obvious pick for any delivery- or distance-themed sibling. auditReport.honestAssessment: Every one of the five ranking pages sells one delivery route and never states its cost in days; this is the only page that puts the Department of Posts' own transit standards (1-2 local, 4-5 rest of India, 4-7 to the USA, customs excluded) next to an instantly delivered name-personalised page, and the only one carrying evidence about cards at all — a BMJ randomised study showing a generic card changes nothing, and a Psychological Science experiment showing writers underestimate how a written message lands. The weaknesses are real: none of the first-party numbers are rakhi-specific (facts.md has no rakhi page type, and the 6.9-hour edit gap is sampled from one romantic template, n=913), only four sources were citable because the genuine card-ritual literature (Emily West's papers) is paywalled and its open copies were retired in April 2025, and Canva's page could not be fetched so one of the five competitors was assessed from SERP data only. Domain authority against Moonpig, Zazzle and Funky Pigeon is not something this post can close, and this is a transactional SERP where retailers own the intent, so treat the realistic upside as answer-engine citation on the 'printed or digital, and will it arrive in time' sub-query rather than the head term. One in-batch convergence to declare: the concurrent C02 post (raksha-bandhan-wishes-with-name-and-photo) also carries a five-item format list, an objection block and a section on what to write next to the name - that overlap is the shared page-structure template plus one genuinely shared sub-question, and it is separated here by anchoring every section to the posted-or-linked card artefact and India Post's transit standards, which that post does not touch.
